title: Which of a district council's 16 treated-water online ammonia channels read more than 0.005 mg/L as N off the water they sample over the fourth quarter of 2027, with the return's laboratory holding times and the hours each plant's chlorine dose ran at its fixed dose
subdomain: sensor-calibration-measurement (three-stream online ammonia analysers: sequencer carryover from the two samples before each reading, apart from the treated water's lagged response, and each analyser's calibration error read as a zero or a span error from its check standard against the raw-water grabs once the raw port's own carryover is taken out)
prompt_shape: 07: the 16 treated channels (eight plants by two waters) each flagged or not, the chart of every channel's offset against the band, and the return's items (b) and (c) by plant
stated_inputs: the 0.005 mg/L as N band, the offset's definition and the return's items in WQ-DS-04 sections 3, 4 and 7

sources.origin: generated by task252/generator/make.py (seeded, deterministic) around a fictional New Zealand district council: eight river-fed water treatment plants, raw water ammonia with rain and dairy-catchment events, the treated water's own response after each plant's transit times, a three-stream colorimetric analyser at each plant whose cell carries part of the two samples before each reading (five of them worn), a zero error and a span error, monthly checks on a flushed cell, the analysers' faults, failed polls reloaded from the plants' PLCs, a lost night in the historian, the weekly sampling round, the courier and a contract laboratory whose analyser keeps standard time; the council, the laboratory and every person are invented, the practice follows published online water quality monitoring practice, and no real dataset is reproduced.
